stem:
The leaves of the old banyan tree outside the college library ______ a deep, glossy green after the monsoon rains.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural noun "leaves", so the verb must be the plural "turn". The phrase "of the old banyan tree" only describes the leaves; matching the verb to "tree" produces the singular forms, which are wrong here.

stem:
Each of the twelve students in Ms. Qureshi's chemistry class ______ a separate notebook for recording experiments.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Each" is the subject and is always singular, so it takes the singular verb "keeps". The plural noun "students" sits inside the phrase "of the twelve students" and does not control the verb, so "keep", "are keeping" and "have kept" all fail.

stem:
Neither the principal nor the teachers ______ willing to move the final examinations to June.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "neither … nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject. The nearer subject is the plural "teachers", so the plural "are" is needed; "is" would agree only with the farther noun, "principal".

stem:
The trunk of handwritten letters, which the museum bought from a family in Multan last year, ______ now on display in the east wing.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular noun "trunk"; both "of handwritten letters" and the clause beginning "which" are interruptions. A singular subject needs "is", not a plural verb chosen to match "letters".

stem:
There ______ several reasons why the bridge over the Ravi was closed for repairs last month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In a sentence beginning with "There", the real subject follows the verb; here it is the plural "several reasons", so the verb must be "are". The singular options treat "There" as the subject, which it is not.

stem:
Playing chess against stronger opponents ______ young players learn to think several moves ahead.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A gerund phrase used as a subject ("Playing chess against stronger opponents") is singular, so it takes "helps". The plural noun "opponents" is the object of a preposition inside the phrase and does not decide the verb.

stem:
At the bottom of the valley, beneath a thick layer of silt and stones, ______ the remains of a settlement that archaeologists date to the Bronze Age.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject, "the remains of a settlement", comes after the verb. "Remains" is plural, so the plural "lie" is correct; the singular options agree wrongly with "silt and stones" or "settlement".

stem:
The report on water quality in the city's three largest lakes ______ that nitrate levels rose sharply between 2018 and 2022.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular "report"; "on water quality in the city's three largest lakes" is a modifying phrase. A singular subject takes "shows", while the other options are plural forms that wrongly match "lakes".

stem:
Mathematics ______ the subject Hamza enjoys most, although he also does well in history.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Mathematics" ends in -s but is a singular noun naming one field of study, so it takes "is". The plural options mistake it for a plural noun.

stem:
The novelist, together with her two translators, ______ expected to attend the literature festival in Karachi next week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Phrases such as "together with her two translators" do not join subjects the way "and" does; the subject remains the singular "novelist", so the verb is "is". "Are" would be correct only if the sentence said "The novelist and her two translators".

stem:
Among the most surprising results of the survey ______ that more than half of the respondents had never visited a public library.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence is inverted, and its subject is the clause "that more than half of the respondents had never visited a public library"; a noun clause is singular, so the verb is "was". The plural "results" is inside the opening prepositional phrase and does not control the verb.

stem:
A number of volunteers from the university ______ helping to clean the beach at Clifton every Sunday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "A number of" means "several" and takes a plural verb, so "are" agrees with "volunteers". Writers often confuse it with "the number of", which is singular.

stem:
The number of students applying to the engineering course ______ grown every year since 2015.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "The number" names a single quantity and is singular, so the verb is "has". "Have" wrongly agrees with "students", which sits inside the phrase "of students applying".

stem:
Bilal and his sister ______ the same bus to school every morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Two subjects joined by "and" make a plural subject, so the verb is "take". The singular forms would agree only with "sister".

stem:
Every painting and sculpture in the gallery ______ a small card beside it that names the artist.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: When "every" introduces subjects joined by "and", each item is considered separately and the verb is singular, so "has" is correct. The pronoun "it" later in the sentence also signals a singular subject; "have" treats the pair as plural.

stem:
The professor's careful analysis of the poems, along with the many footnotes she added to the new edition, ______ the book valuable to students.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular "analysis"; the phrase "along with the many footnotes…" is an interruption, not part of the subject. A singular subject needs "makes", while "make" wrongly agrees with "poems" or "footnotes".

stem:
Only one of the five proposals submitted by the design teams ______ the city's requirements for cost and safety.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is "one", which is singular, so the verb is "meets". The plurals "proposals" and "teams" sit inside modifying phrases and do not control the verb.

stem:
The instructions printed on the back of the box ______ easy to follow, even for first-time users.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural "instructions", so the verb is "are". The singular choices match "back" or "box", which are objects of prepositions.

stem:
The sound of the waves crashing against the rocks below the cliffs ______ visitors to the lighthouse long before they reach the top.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Strip away the modifiers and the core is "The sound … greets visitors"; "sound" is singular, so the verb is "greets". The plural forms are drawn in by "waves", "rocks" and "cliffs", none of which is the subject.

stem:
Either the Lahore office or the Islamabad office ______ responsible for processing the new visa applications.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "either … or", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, here the singular "Islamabad office", so "is" is correct. "Are" would treat the two offices as a combined plural subject, which "or" does not create.

stem:
The birds that nest along the shore of the lake ______ south every autumn.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural "birds"; "that nest along the shore of the lake" describes them. A plural subject takes "fly", while "flies" wrongly agrees with "shore" or "lake".

stem:
The economist argued that rising rents in the city's older districts, rather than higher fuel prices, ______ the main reason families are moving to the suburbs.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject of the clause is the plural "rising rents"; "rather than higher fuel prices" is an interrupting phrase that does not add to the subject. A plural subject needs "are", so the singular forms fail.

stem:
The stack of exam papers on Mr. Rizvi's desk ______ taller every few minutes as students hand in their scripts.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular "stack", so the verb is "grows". "Grow" and the other plural forms wrongly agree with "papers", the object of the preposition "of".

stem:
Everyone in the two villages ______ access to the new health clinic.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Indefinite pronouns ending in -one, such as "everyone", are singular, so the verb is "has". The plural "villages" is inside a prepositional phrase and does not change that.

stem:
Some of the water stored in the reservoir ______ lost to evaporation during the hottest months.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Some" takes its number from the noun it refers to; here that noun is "water", which is uncountable and therefore singular, so "is" is correct. The plural forms would suit a countable plural such as "Some of the pipes".

stem:
"Tales of the Indus", a collection of short stories by a young writer from Sukkur, ______ won two national awards.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The title of a single book is singular even when its words are plural, so the verb is "has". "Have" mistakes the plural-looking title (or the word "stories") for the subject.

stem:
The tortoise pulled ______ head into its shell as soon as the children came near.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The possessive form of "it" is "its", with no apostrophe, and it matches the singular "tortoise". "It's" means "it is", "its'" is not a word, and "their" is plural.

stem:
After two years of fieldwork in Chitral, the scientists finally published ______ findings in an international journal.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The antecedent, "scientists", is plural, so the plural possessive "their" is needed. "There" names a place, "they're" means "they are", and "its" is singular.

stem:
The prize money was divided equally between Sana and ______, since we had written the winning essay together.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After a preposition such as "between", a pronoun must be in the object case, so "me" is correct. "I" is a subject pronoun, a common error in pairs like this, and "myself" is reflexive, which needs "I" earlier in the clause as its subject.

stem:
My brother and ______ spent the summer volunteering at a clinic in Gilgit.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun is part of the subject of "spent", so it must be the subject form "I". Removing "My brother and" shows the test: "I spent the summer", not "me spent" or "myself spent".

stem:
The engineer ______ inspected the bridge last spring found several cracks in its supports.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun is the subject of "inspected", so the subject form "who" is needed. "Whom" is an object form, "which" is not used for people, and "whose" shows possession.

stem:
Rivers flowing out of the Himalayas carry huge amounts of silt and deposit ______ on the plains when the water slows down.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun stands for "silt", an uncountable singular noun, and it is the object of "deposit", so "it" is correct. "Them" wrongly refers back to "rivers" or "amounts", and "they" and "its" are the wrong case.

stem:
Before starting the project, the two researchers taught ______ to read the old Persian script in which the records were kept.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: When the object refers to the same people as the subject, a reflexive pronoun is needed; for the plural "researchers" that is "themselves". "Theirselves" is not standard English, "itself" is singular, and "them" would suggest other people.

stem:
______ students in the final year were given an extra week to complete our research projects.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun begins the subject of "were given", so the subject form "We" is correct; dropping "students" shows this ("We were given"). "Us" is an object form and "Ourselves" is reflexive.

stem:
The author, ______ latest novel is set in the old city of Peshawar, will speak at the book fair on Saturday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Whose" is the possessive relative pronoun: the novel belongs to the author. "Who's" is a contraction of "who is", which makes no sense before "latest novel".

stem:
The old city walls are still standing, although ______ were badly damaged by an earthquake in the nineteenth century.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural "walls" and is the subject of "were", so "they" is correct. "It" and "this" are singular and do not agree with "walls" or with "were".

stem:
The violinist and the pianist rehearsed separately for weeks, but on the night of the concert ______ performance together was flawless.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The possessive refers to two people, "the violinist and the pianist", so the plural possessive "their" is needed. "Its" is singular, "there" is an adverb of place and "they're" means "they are".

stem:
Since 2019, the small bakery on Mall Road ______ fresh naan for the hostel every morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Since 2019" describes an action that began in the past and continues to the present, which calls for the present perfect "has supplied". The simple present and simple past do not fit an expression of time beginning with "since".

stem:
By the time the fire engines reached the warehouse, the flames ______ to the second floor.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "By the time" with a past event ("reached") requires the past perfect for the action completed before it, so "had spread" is correct. "Have spread" links the action to the present, and "will spread" is future.

stem:
Last year, the botanists ______ more than 300 seed samples from the forests of Swat.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Last year" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "collected" is correct. The present perfect "have collected" cannot be used with a finished time expression like "last year".

stem:
Next March, Ayesha ______ at the children's hospital for exactly ten years.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence describes a period that will be complete at a future point ("Next March"), so the future perfect "will have worked" is needed. "Has worked" measures time up to now, not up to a future date.

stem:
The children had ______ their bicycles all the way to the lake and back before lunch.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After the helping verb "had", the past participle is required, and the past participle of "ride" is "ridden". "Rode" is the simple past form and cannot follow "had".

stem:
The well behind the old mosque had ______ dry by the end of the summer, so villagers carried water from the river.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Had" must be followed by a past participle; the participle of "go" is "gone". "Went" is the simple past, so "had went" is a common but non-standard form.

stem:
After the long climb to the fort, the tired hikers ______ down in the shade of a tree to rest.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The verb meaning "to recline" is "lie", and its past tense is "lay". "Laid" is the past of "lay" (to put something down), which needs an object; "lied" means told an untruth, and "layed" is not a word.

stem:
When the train finally pulled into Rawalpindi station, Nida grabbed her bag and ______ onto the crowded platform.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence narrates finished events in the simple past ("pulled", "grabbed"), so the verb paired with "grabbed" should also be past: "stepped". The other forms switch tense without reason.

stem:
If the bridge had been inspected earlier, the engineers ______ the cracks before they grew so large.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: This is a condition about the past that did not happen ("had been inspected"), so the result clause needs "would have" plus a past participle. "Would find" refers to the present or future, and "had found" is not a result form.

stem:
If the rain ______ until tomorrow afternoon, the cricket final will be moved to Saturday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In a condition about the future, the "if" clause takes the simple present and the main clause takes "will", so "continues" is correct. Putting "will" in the "if" clause is a common error, and "continued" or "would continue" belong to unreal conditions, not to a sentence with "will be moved".

stem:
Pure water ______ at 100 °C at sea level, but on a high mountain it boils at a lower temperature.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A general scientific fact is expressed in the simple present, and the second clause ("it boils") confirms this, so "boils" is correct. The past forms present a permanent truth as a single past event.

stem:
When the archaeologists entered the tomb, they discovered that someone ______ it centuries earlier.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The opening of the tomb happened before the past moment of discovery, so the past perfect "had opened" is required. "Has opened" connects the action to the present, which clashes with "centuries earlier".

stem:
The concert had already ______ by the time we found our seats in the hall.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After "had", the past participle is needed, and the participle of "begin" is "begun". "Began" is the simple past form, so "had began" is incorrect.

stem:
The new traffic rules, which ______ into effect last week, require all buses to stop only at marked points.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Last week" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "came" is required. The present perfect "have come" cannot be combined with a specific past time such as "last week".

stem:
Visitors to the archive must ______ their bags and coats at the entrance.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A modal verb such as "must" is always followed by the base form of a verb, so "leave" is correct. "Must left", "must leaving" and "must to leave" are not standard.

stem:
The students are looking forward to ______ the new observatory in the hills next month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In "look forward to", the word "to" is a preposition, so it is followed by a gerund: "visiting". Treating "to" as part of an infinitive leads to the error "look forward to visit".

stem:
Ahmed told me yesterday that he ______ the novel twice before he saw the film.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The reading took place before another past event ("he saw the film"), and the whole report is in the past ("told"), so the past perfect "had read" is correct. "Has read" and "reads" anchor the action in the present.

stem:
The laboratory ______ its first clinical trial three years ago with only four researchers.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Three years ago" names a finished time in the past, which requires the simple past "began". The present perfect "has begun" cannot be used with "ago", and the past perfect "had begun" needs a later past event to refer back from.

stem:
Historians believe that the fort ______ in the sixteenth century, although some of its walls are much older.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The fort received the action of building, so a passive verb is needed, and the time ("in the sixteenth century") is finished, so the simple past passive "was built" is correct. "Had built" is active and would mean the fort built something.

stem:
Each spring, the almond trees in the valley ______, and visitors travel from far away to see them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Each spring" describes a repeated, habitual event, and the parallel clause uses the present ("visitors travel"), so the simple present "blossom" fits. The past forms clash with "travel".

stem:
The study, which ______ over a period of six years, found that children who read aloud every day developed larger vocabularies.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A study does not conduct anything; it is conducted by researchers, so the passive "was conducted" is needed. The active forms "conducted", "has conducted" and "is conducting" would wrongly make the study the doer and leave the verb without an object.

stem:
The letter, written in 1947 and ______ for decades in a family trunk, was donated to the city archive last month.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The blank is joined by "and" to the past participle "written", so it must also be a past participle: "hidden". "Was hidden" adds a second main verb inside the phrase, and "hid" and "hiding" break the parallel form and wrongly make the letter the doer.

stem:
Of the two routes to Naran, the road through the valley is ______, although the mountain road offers better views.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: When exactly two things are compared, the comparative form ("safer") is used, so "the safer" is correct. "Safest" and "most safe" are superlatives, which are used for three or more things.

stem:
Before the final match, all eleven ______ shirts were washed and pressed by the team's kit manager.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The shirts belong to eleven players, so the plural possessive is needed: add an apostrophe after the plural -s to get "players'". "Player's" is singular possessive, and "players" is a plain plural that shows no ownership.

stem:
After the storm, ______ only bridge to the main road was rebuilt with money from the district. The village had been cut off for a week.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The second sentence makes clear that there is one village, so the singular possessive "the village's" is correct. "The villages'" is plural possessive, and "the villages" and "the village" show no possession.

stem:
The playground was covered with the ______ toys after the school's annual fun fair.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Children" is already plural, so its possessive is formed by adding 's: "children's". "Childrens" is not a word, so "childrens'" and "childrens" are both incorrect.

stem:
Zainab borrowed her only ______ car to drive her grandparents to the airport.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Only" shows that she has one brother, so the singular possessive "brother's" is correct. "Brothers'" would mean the car belongs to several brothers, and "brothers" is a plain plural.

stem:
The conference in Hyderabad focused on ______ access to higher education in rural Sindh.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Women" is an irregular plural, so its possessive adds 's: "women's". "Womens" does not exist in standard English, which rules out "womens'" and "womens".

stem:
The aurora, seen in the far north and far south, is one of the most striking natural ______ on Earth.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "One of the most striking natural…" requires a plural noun, and the plural of "phenomenon" is "phenomena". "Phenomenon" is singular, "phenomenons" is non-standard, and "phenomena's" is a possessive with nothing to possess.

stem:
The judges used three ______ to score each essay: clarity, originality and accuracy.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Three" calls for a plural, and the plural of "criterion" is "criteria". "Criterion" is singular, "criterions" is non-standard, and "criteria's" is a possessive form.

stem:
In the hills above Murree, two ______ worth of rain fell in a single afternoon.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: In expressions of time and amount such as "two weeks' worth", the time word takes a possessive; since "two weeks" is plural, the apostrophe follows the s. "Week's" is singular and does not match "two".

stem:
For three generations, ______ dairy farm has supplied the town with fresh milk; Mr. and Mrs. Khan now run it with their four children.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The farm belongs to the Khan family, referred to as "the Khans"; the plural possessive of a family name adds an apostrophe after the s: "the Khans'". "The Khan's" refers to a single person, and "the Khans" shows no possession.

stem:
Several new ______ have opened along the canal road this year, each selling bread and sweets.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence needs a plain plural subject for "have opened", and nouns ending in a consonant plus -y change the y to -ies: "bakeries". The apostrophe forms are possessives, and "bakerys" is misspelled.

stem:
Our measurements matched ______ almost exactly, even though the two groups used different equipment.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The possessive pronoun that stands alone is "theirs", which never takes an apostrophe. "There's" means "there is", and "their's" and "theirs'" are not standard forms.

stem:
After speed cameras were installed, there were ______ accidents on the motorway than in any previous year.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Accidents" is a countable plural noun, so it takes "fewer"; "less" is used with uncountable nouns such as "traffic" or "noise". "Lesser" and "little" do not form a comparison with "than" here.

stem:
By the end of the exam, the students had so little time left that they ______ answer the final question.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Hardly" is already negative in meaning, so it must not be combined with "not"; "could hardly" is correct. The other choices create double negatives.

stem:
Walking along the beach at sunset, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Imran noticed a starfish stranded on the wet sand.
the wet sand had a starfish stranded on it that Imran saw.
a starfish stranded on the wet sand caught Imran's eye.
a stranded starfish was noticed by Imran on the wet sand.
explanation: An introductory modifier must be followed by the noun it describes. Imran is the one walking, so the main clause must begin with "Imran"; the other choices make the starfish or the sand do the walking.

stem:
Known for its carved wooden balconies and narrow lanes, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: there are many students of architecture who visit Peshawar's old city.
students of architecture often visit the old city of Peshawar.
many students of architecture are attracted to the old city of Peshawar.
the old city of Peshawar attracts many students of architecture.
explanation: The phrase "Known for its carved wooden balconies…" describes the old city, so "the old city of Peshawar" must come right after the comma. The other choices place "students" or "there" there, so the students seem to have the balconies.

stem:
After finishing her first marathon, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Sara's legs ached for two days.
it took Sara two days to walk normally again.
a deep ache stayed in Sara's legs for two days.
Sara could barely walk for two days.
explanation: Sara finished the marathon, so "Sara" must be the subject immediately after the modifier. In "Sara's legs ached", the subject is "legs", and the legs did not finish the marathon; "it" and "a deep ache" fail the same way.

stem:
A gifted mathematician from Tehran, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: it was in 2014 that Maryam Mirzakhani became the first woman to win the Fields Medal.
Maryam Mirzakhani became the first woman to win the Fields Medal in 2014.
the Fields Medal went to Maryam Mirzakhani in 2014, making her its first female winner.
Maryam Mirzakhani's work earned her the Fields Medal in 2014.
explanation: The appositive "A gifted mathematician from Tehran" must sit next to the person it renames, so the main clause must open with "Maryam Mirzakhani". In the possessive choice the subject is "work", and the other choices begin with "the Fields Medal" or "it".

stem:
To qualify for the school relay team, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: under thirteen seconds is the time needed to run the sprint.
running the sprint in under thirteen seconds is required.
a runner must run the sprint in under thirteen seconds.
the qualifying time for the sprint is under thirteen seconds.
explanation: An introductory infinitive phrase must be followed by the person who performs the action; only a runner can qualify for the team. The other choices make an action, a time or a requirement qualify for the team.

stem:
As a child growing up in Quetta, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the writer spent long winter evenings reading by the fire.
long winter evenings were spent by the writer reading by the fire.
the writer's winter evenings were spent reading by the fire.
reading by the fire filled the writer's long winter evenings.
explanation: "As a child growing up in Quetta" describes the writer, so "the writer" must be the subject. The possessive "the writer's" is a trap: the subject of that clause is "evenings", which did not grow up in Quetta.

stem:
Exhausted after the twelve-hour journey from Skardu, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: sleep came to the climbers as soon as they reached the hotel.
the climbers fell asleep as soon as they reached the hotel.
the hotel beds were a welcome sight for the climbers.
the climbers' first act at the hotel was to fall asleep.
explanation: The climbers were exhausted, so "the climbers" must follow the introductory phrase. The other choices make sleep, the beds or the climbers' "first act" exhausted.

stem:
Unlike most birds, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: penguins' wings work as flippers rather than for flight.
the wings of penguins are used for swimming rather than flying.
penguins cannot fly but are excellent swimmers.
flying is impossible for penguins, which swim instead.
explanation: "Unlike most birds" sets up a comparison with another kind of bird, so the subject must be "penguins". Comparing birds with "the wings of penguins", "flying" or "penguins' wings" is illogical.

stem:
Because it lies in the path of the monsoon, Murree receives far more rain each year than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence compares two places that receive rain, so the comparison needs a place and a matching verb: "than Multan does". "That of Multan" and "Multan's does" have no noun for "that" or "Multan's" to stand for, and "Multan's rainfall is" compares a city with rainfall.

stem:
Like her mentor, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the poet Hira Baig writes verse that blends Urdu and Punjabi.
Hira Baig's poems blend Urdu and Punjabi.
blending Urdu and Punjabi is typical of Hira Baig's poetry.
the poetry of Hira Baig blends Urdu and Punjabi.
explanation: "Like her mentor" compares a person with a person, so the subject must be the poet herself. The other choices compare the mentor with poetry, poems or an action, which is an illogical comparison.

stem:
Completed in 1673 on the orders of the emperor Aurangzeb, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the builders placed the Badshahi Mosque opposite the Lahore Fort.
the Badshahi Mosque stands opposite the Lahore Fort.
visitors to the Badshahi Mosque can see the Lahore Fort across the square.
there is a clear view of the Lahore Fort from the Badshahi Mosque.
explanation: The introductory phrase describes the mosque, so "the Badshahi Mosque" must be the subject that follows it. The other choices make visitors, "there" or the builders the thing completed in 1673.

stem:
Having studied harvest records from forty farms for two seasons, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the team concluded that the new seed variety raised wheat yields.
it became clear to the team that the new seed variety raised wheat yields.
the conclusion of the team was that the new seed variety raised wheat yields.
the new seed variety was shown by the team to raise wheat yields.
explanation: The team did the studying, so "the team" must be the subject right after the modifier. In the other choices the subject is "the conclusion", "it" or "the new seed variety", none of which studied the records.

stem:
While searching through old newspapers in the city archive, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: a letter from 1919 was discovered by a historian.
a forgotten letter from 1919 caught a historian's attention.
the discovery of a forgotten 1919 letter was made by a historian.
a historian came across a forgotten letter from 1919.
explanation: The person searching must be the subject after "While searching…", so "a historian" must come first. The other choices make the letter or "the discovery" do the searching.

stem:
Founded in 1984 by a group of retired teachers, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: more than 2,000 students now attend the school.
today there are more than 2,000 students at the school.
the school's students now number more than 2,000.
the school now has more than 2,000 students.
explanation: The school was founded, so "the school" must be the subject immediately after the phrase. The possessive "the school's students" makes "students" the subject, and students were not founded in 1984.

stem:
Using a simple telescope that he had built himself, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: Galileo observed four of Jupiter's moons in 1610.
the first observation of Jupiter's moons was made by Galileo in 1610.
Jupiter's four largest moons were first seen by Galileo in 1610.
four of Jupiter's moons were observed by Galileo in 1610.
explanation: Galileo used the telescope, so "Galileo" must be the subject after the opening phrase. The other choices make moons or an observation use the telescope.

stem:
Originally written in Persian, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: a scholar translated the poem into Urdu in the nineteenth century.
the poem was translated into Urdu in the nineteenth century.
an Urdu translation of the poem appeared in the nineteenth century.
Urdu readers first read the poem in the nineteenth century.
explanation: The poem was written in Persian, so "the poem" must follow the modifier. The other choices make a scholar, a translation or readers "originally written in Persian".

stem:
Unlike the mountains of the north, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the plains of Punjab are flat and fertile.
Punjab has plains that are flat and fertile.
there are flat and fertile plains in Punjab.
Punjab's farmers work on flat, fertile plains.
explanation: The comparison must be between like things: mountains and plains. The other choices compare the mountains with Punjab, with "there", or with farmers.

stem:
On weekends, Hassan enjoys reading, swimming and ______ meals for his family.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Items in a list should share the same grammatical form. "Reading" and "swimming" are gerunds, so the third item must be "cooking"; "to cook" and "he cooks" break the pattern.

stem:
The new library on campus is spacious, well lit and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The list follows "is" and contains adjectives ("spacious", "well lit"), so the last item must also be an adjective: "quiet". "Quietly" is an adverb, and the other two choices add a new verb.

stem:
The goals of the recycling project are to reduce waste, to save energy and ______ small local businesses.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The list repeats "to" before each item ("to reduce", "to save"), so the third item must be "to support". A gerund, a noun phrase or a present-tense verb breaks the parallel structure.

stem:
The coach told the players that they should arrive early, warm up properly and ______ during team talks.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: All three actions follow "should", so each must be a base verb: "arrive", "warm up" and "listen". Adding "to", "-ing" or a new subject breaks the series.

stem:
Becoming fluent in a new language depends less on studying grammar rules than ______ with native speakers every day.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The comparison "less on … than …" needs the same structure on both sides, so "on studying" must be matched by "on talking". Without "on", the sentence compares a prepositional phrase with a bare gerund.

stem:
The food festival in Lahore was praised not only for its music but also ______ the variety of its food stalls.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "not only … but also", the words after each part must match. The first part is "for its music", so the second must also begin with "for"; the other prepositions break the pairing.

stem:
The trainer advised Saima to drink more water, to sleep at least seven hours a night and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The list after "advised Saima" uses infinitives ("to drink", "to sleep"), so the last item must be "to avoid". A gerund or a clause does not match the other two items.

stem:
The researchers found that students who read for pleasure scored higher in vocabulary tests, wrote more fluently and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: their confidence in class discussions was higher.
having more confidence in class discussions.
were more confident in class discussions.
explanation: The three items share the subject "students who read for pleasure" and must all be past-tense verb phrases: "scored", "wrote" and "were". The other choices offer a participle, a noun phrase or a new clause with its own subject.

stem:
The museum's guided tour includes a walk through the gardens, a visit to the old printing press and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: a talk by the head curator.
the head curator gives a talk.
explanation: Each item in the list is a noun phrase beginning with "a" ("a walk", "a visit"), so the last one should be "a talk by the head curator". The other choices switch to a gerund, a clause or an infinitive.

stem:
For many students, studying early in the morning is more effective than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A comparison with "than" should set like forms side by side; "studying early in the morning" is a gerund phrase, so it must be compared with "studying late at night". The infinitive and the clause are not parallel.

stem:
The engineer's report recommended widening the main road, adding a cycle lane and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the speed limit should be lowered.
explanation: "Recommended" is followed by a series of gerund phrases ("widening", "adding"), so the third item must be "lowering the speed limit". An infinitive, a clause or a plain noun phrase breaks the parallel form.

stem:
The city's transport plan aims to make buses cheaper, faster and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The words after "make buses" are comparative adjectives ("cheaper", "faster"), so the third must be "more reliable". "More reliability" is a noun, "reliably" is an adverb, and "it more reliable" adds an extra pronoun.

stem:
What impressed the judges most was not the size of the robot but ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "not … but", both parts must have the same form. "The size of the robot" is a noun phrase, so it must be matched by "the speed of its responses"; a gerund, a clause or an adjective phrase does not pair with it.

stem:
The keys to the chemistry laboratory ______ kept in a locked box in the staff room.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural "keys"; "to the chemistry laboratory" only describes them. A plural subject needs "are", while the singular options wrongly agree with "laboratory".

stem:
The scholar to ______ the manuscript was sent replied within a week with a full translation.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun is the object of the preposition "to", so the object form "whom" is required. "Who" is a subject form, "which" is not used for people, and "whose" shows possession.

stem:
After testing the rock in the hills, the engineers decided ______ the opening of the tunnel by six months.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The verb "decide" is followed by an infinitive, so "decided to delay" is correct. "Decided delaying", "decided delay" and "decided delayed" are not standard.

stem:
If ______ planning to visit the Lahore Fort, arrive early to avoid the afternoon crowds.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence needs a subject and a verb ("you are planning"), and the contraction of "you are" is "you're". "Your" is a possessive, and the other two are misspellings.

stem:
The quality of the photographs taken by the two drones ______ surprisingly high for such small cameras.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular "quality"; "of the photographs taken by the two drones" is a modifying phrase. A singular subject takes "is", so the plural forms that match "photographs" or "drones" are wrong.

stem:
Had the ferry left port on time, the passengers ______ Gwadar before dark.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Had the ferry left…" is an inverted form of "If the ferry had left", a condition about the past that did not happen. The result therefore needs "would have" plus a past participle; "would reach" refers to the present or future.

stem:
In Hunza, many apricot farmers dry ______ fruit on flat rooftops during the summer.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The antecedent is the plural "farmers", so the plural possessive "their" is correct. "There" is an adverb, "they're" means "they are", and "its" is singular.

stem:
Determined to finish before dark, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the volunteers planted the last row of saplings by six o'clock.
six o'clock saw the volunteers plant the last row of saplings.
the planting of the last row of saplings ended by six o'clock.
the last row of saplings was planted by the volunteers by six o'clock.
explanation: Only people can be determined, so "the volunteers" must be the subject after the opening phrase. The other choices make the saplings, the planting or the time determined.

stem:
Hidden among the reeds at the edge of the lake ______ a small wooden boat and two oars.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence is inverted; its subject, "a small wooden boat and two oars", comes after the verb. Two nouns joined by "and" form a plural subject, so the verb is "were"; "was" agrees only with "boat".

stem:
Please ______ the boxes of books on the table by the door so that the volunteers can sort them.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Set" means "to place something" and takes an object, here "the boxes". "Sit" means "to be seated" and cannot take an object, "sat" is its past form, and "setting" cannot follow "Please" as a command.

stem:
Over the past decade, the salaries of nurses in the region have risen faster than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence compares salaries with salaries, so a pronoun must stand for "salaries"; since the noun is plural, "those of teachers" is correct. "Teachers" and "teachers have" compare salaries with people, and "that" is singular.

stem:
The results of the national science competition will ______ on Friday morning.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Results do not announce anything; they are announced, so a passive form is needed, and after "will" the passive is "be announced". "Will announced" and "will been announced" are not standard, and "will announcing" is not a verb form.

stem:
The new forest policy is designed both to protect old trees and ______ for people in nearby villages.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "both … and", the two parts must match: "to protect" is an infinitive, so the second part must be "to create jobs". A gerund, a noun phrase or a clause breaks the pairing.

stem:
Karachi is the largest city in the country: its population is greater than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: that of any other city in Pakistan.
those of any other city in Pakistan.
that of any city in Pakistan.
explanation: A population must be compared with another population, so "that of" is needed, and "other" is required because Karachi is itself a city in Pakistan. "Any other city" compares a population with a city, and "those" is plural.

stem:
Saad was cooking dinner in the kitchen when the power suddenly ______.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A past continuous action ("was cooking") interrupted by a single event takes the simple past for that event, so "went out" is correct. The present and future forms do not fit a past narrative.

stem:
After the flood, a large ______ of sand and mud had to be cleared from the main road.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Sand and mud" are uncountable nouns, so they are measured with "amount". "Number" is used with countable plurals such as "rocks", and "many" and "few" are not nouns here.

stem:
Because the two sisters had studied together for months, the teacher was not surprised that ______ answers were almost identical.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The answers belong to both sisters, so the plural possessive "their" is needed. "Her" refers to one person only and "its" is used for things, while "there" is an adverb of place.

stem:
The blue cups on the top shelf of the cupboard ______ to my grandmother.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the plural "cups", so the verb is "belong". The singular forms wrongly agree with "shelf" or "cupboard", which are objects of prepositions.

stem:
Neither the manager nor her assistants ______ aware that the meeting had been moved to Tuesday.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "neither … nor", the verb agrees with the nearer subject, the plural "assistants", so "were" is correct. "Was" would agree only with the farther subject, "manager".

stem:
Reading the comments under online news articles rarely ______ anyone's mood.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: A gerund phrase used as a subject ("Reading the comments under online news articles") is singular, so the verb is "improves". The plural forms wrongly agree with "comments" or "articles", which sit inside the phrase.

stem:
Beside the entrance to the old library ______ two stone lions carved in the 1890s.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence is inverted: the subject, "two stone lions", follows the verb. A plural subject needs "stand"; the singular forms agree wrongly with "entrance" or "library".

stem:
Several of the participants in the sleep study ______ been contacted again for a follow-up interview.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Several" is always plural, so it takes "have". The singular forms ignore that "several" refers to more than one participant.

stem:
Before the match, the coach asked Fahad and ______ to lead the warm-up.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun is an object of "asked", so the object form "me" is needed; dropping "Fahad and" shows this ("asked me"). "I" is a subject form, and "myself" needs "I" as the subject of the clause.

stem:
At the end of the evening, the award was presented to ______ volunteers who had run the fundraiser.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After the preposition "to", the object form is needed, so "us volunteers" is correct; removing "volunteers" gives "presented to us". "We" is a subject form, and "ourselves" needs "we" as the subject.

stem:
The new hospital wing has ______ own backup generator in case of power cuts.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The possessive form of "it" is "its", without an apostrophe, and it matches the singular "wing". "It's" means "it is" or "it has", and "its'" does not exist.

stem:
The scholars ______ translated the old diaries spent four years on the project.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun is the subject of "translated" and refers to people, so "who" is correct. "Which" is used for things, "whom" is an object form, and "whose" is possessive.

stem:
When the students handed in their forms, the clerk checked ______ carefully for errors.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The pronoun refers to the plural "forms" and is the object of "checked", so "them" is correct. "It" is singular and "they" is a subject form.

stem:
By the end of the summer camp, every child had ______ across the pool at least once.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After "had", the past participle is required, and the participle of "swim" is "swum". "Swam" is the simple past, and "swimmed" is not a standard form.

stem:
The scientist set the soil samples on the bench and let them ______ undisturbed for an hour.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Let" is followed by the base form of a verb, and the verb meaning "to remain in a flat position" is "lie". "Lay" means "to put something down" and needs an object, while "laid" and "lain" are participles that cannot follow "let them".

stem:
For the past ten years, the clinic ______ free eye tests to schoolchildren in the district.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "For the past ten years" describes a period that runs up to now, so the present perfect "has offered" is required. The simple past would suggest the period has ended, and the simple present does not express duration.

stem:
If Bilal ______ more free time, he would learn to play the sitar.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: This is an unreal present condition, shown by "would learn" in the main clause, so the "if" clause takes the simple past, "had". "Has" and "will have" belong to real conditions, and "would" does not go in the "if" clause.

stem:
Yesterday, the bus from Murree ______ twenty minutes late because of the heavy rain.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Yesterday" marks a finished past time, so the simple past "arrived" is correct. The present perfect cannot be used with "yesterday".

stem:
The pottery, shaped by hand and ______ in a wood-fired kiln, is sold at the Sunday market.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The blank is joined by "and" to the past participle "shaped", so it must also be a past participle: "baked". "Was baked" adds a second main verb inside the interrupting phrase, and "bakes" and "baking" break the parallel form.

stem:
During the tour, the children were told not ______ the paintings in the gallery.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Told" is followed by an infinitive ("told someone to do something"), and the negative form is "not to touch". The other forms do not fit after "were told not".

stem:
Before the parade, the two ______ manes were braided with red ribbons.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The manes belong to two horses, so the plural possessive "horses'" is needed. "Horse's" is singular, and "horses" shows no possession.

stem:
Dr. Malik is an old friend of ______, so I asked her to read my essay.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: After "a friend of", English uses the independent possessive pronoun: "a friend of mine". "My" must be followed by a noun, "me" shows no possession, and "mine's" is not a word.

stem:
______ been raining in Islamabad since early morning, so the match may be called off.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The sentence needs a subject and a helping verb ("It has been raining"), and "It's" is the contraction of "it has". "Its" is a possessive, "Its'" does not exist, and "Its has" uses the possessive where a subject is needed.

stem:
The museum's new gallery displays nine ______ of fish found only in the Indus river system.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Species" has the same form in the singular and the plural, so "nine species" is correct. "Specie" is a different word meaning coins, "specieses" does not exist, and "species'" is possessive.

stem:
As the oldest of five siblings, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the younger brothers often got homework help from Kamran.
Kamran's evenings were often spent helping his younger brothers.
Kamran often helped his younger brothers with their homework.
helping his younger brothers with homework was often Kamran's job.
explanation: "As the oldest of five siblings" describes Kamran, so "Kamran" must be the subject. In "Kamran's evenings" the subject is "evenings", and the other choices make an action or the younger brothers the oldest sibling.

stem:
Reaching the summit just after dawn, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: the sun rose over the glacier as the climbers watched.
the view of the glacier at sunrise amazed the climbers.
the climbers watched the sun rise over the glacier.
the climbers' cameras captured the sunrise over the glacier.
explanation: The climbers reached the summit, so "the climbers" must follow the opening phrase. The other choices make the sun, the view or the cameras reach the summit.

stem:
Rich in iron and protein, ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
options: many Pakistani families eat lentils every day.
Pakistani cooks use lentils in many dishes.
there are lentil dishes in many Pakistani homes.
lentils are a daily food in many Pakistani homes.
explanation: The phrase "Rich in iron and protein" describes lentils, so "lentils" must be the subject after the comma. The other choices make families, cooks or "there" rich in iron and protein.

stem:
According to the reviewers, the battery of the new phone lasts much longer than ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The battery must be compared with another battery, so "that of the older model" is needed; "that" is singular to match "battery". "The older model" and "the older model does" compare a battery with a phone, and "those" is plural.

stem:
The scholarship money can be spent either on tuition fees or ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: With "either … or", the two parts must match. "On tuition fees" is a prepositional phrase, so the second part must also be one: "on books".

stem:
Bilal enjoys hiking in the summer and ______ in the winter.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Both activities are objects of "enjoys", which takes gerunds, so "hiking" must be matched by "skiing". "Enjoys … to ski" is not standard, and "ski" and "skied" are not parallel.

stem:
The workshop teaches students how to plan an experiment, how to record data and ______

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: Each item in the series is a phrase beginning with "how to", so the third should be "how to present their results". A gerund, a noun phrase or a clause breaks the series.

stem:
The cost of repairing the two bridges damaged in the floods ______ been estimated at Rs 40 million.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: The subject is the singular "cost"; everything from "of repairing" to "floods" modifies it. A singular subject takes "has", while "have" agrees wrongly with "bridges" or "floods".

stem:
This year the factory used ______ water than it did in 2020, thanks to a new recycling system.

Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?
explanation: "Water" is uncountable, so the comparative is "less"; "fewer" is used only with countable plurals such as "bottles" or "cups". "Lesser" means "smaller in importance", and "little" cannot be followed by "than".
